text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Algirdas Brazauskas, currently visiting Brussels, was assured during his meeting with Javier Solana, NATO secretary general, that Lithuania has not been crossed off the list of future NATO members.

- A search was carried out in the apartment of Zigmas Skirkevicius, a representative of the government of the northern Panevezhys region, as well as in the apartment of his two sons. The latter are accused of producing fake police, advocates and customs seals. Skirkevicius will inform the government and then after consultations will make a decision whether to resign.

- Alleged former KGB agent Julius Slavin has been accused of the genocide of the Lithuanian population after World War Two. The prosecutor's office has brought a case against Slavin, who is 72 and currently lives in Germany, and is going to apply to Germany to deport him.

- During the last four years the number of people who show absolutely no interest in politics has gone up three fold. Only 25 percent of the population know who represents their area in parliament. Only seven percent of those who participated in the opinion poll are ready to re-elect the same people.

- Juozas Antanavicius, spiritual leader of Lithuanian Union of Catholic Women, said his group was shocked by the use of a fragment of a picture of the Sistine Madonna by Raphael for the campaign leaflets of the Lithuanian Womens Party, led by former prime minister Kazimiera Prunskiene.

- An interview with Richardas Vaigauskas, a former Soviet spy and KGB colonel, claims Russia still has a strong interest in Lithuania and that Lithuania also attracts the intelligence services of other countries.
